summary:
Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory. The Equality Act 2010 of the United Kingdom and its 2025 single-sex services code do not automatically extend to Bermuda. Local legislation governs, and United Kingdom measures could be applied to Bermuda only by Order in Council.

There is no legal recognition of transgender people in Bermuda. By omission, there is no protection from discrimination for transgender people. The ability of persons to express gender identity is described as often difficult.

The Human Rights Act 1981, as amended by Parliament in 2013, prohibits discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation. That prohibition does not extend to gender identity. A trans visitor therefore has no explicit statutory protection under that Act.

Prior to 1994 anal sex and oral sex were illegal and punishable by up to ten years imprisonment, while lesbian activity was never illegal. On 14 May 1994 the House of Assembly voted 22 to 16 to decriminalise consensual sex between adult men, removing two sections of the Criminal Code through the 1994 Stubbs Bill. That reform legalised consensual sexual conduct in private but retained an unequal age of consent of 18 for gay male conduct versus 16 for heterosexual and lesbian conduct, described as in clear violation of the European Convention on Human Rights.

On 1 November 2019 an amendment to the Criminal Code set 18 years for consensual anal intercourse. As of 2022 the age remains unequal at 18 for anal intercourse versus 16 for other sexual activity. The provision on gross indecency between men was repealed in 2019.

Same-sex marriage was first made legal by Supreme Court ruling in May 2017 finding the Marriage Act 1944 inconsistent with the Human Rights Act. It was then replaced by domestic partnerships under a law passed in December 2017, given royal assent on 7 February 2018 and effective 1 June 2018. The Supreme Court restored same-sex marriage on 6 June 2018 and the Court of Appeal upheld that restoration on 23 November 2018. On 14 March 2022 the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council banned same-sex marriage again, with laws in July 2022 retrospectively backdating legality for the period prior to March 2022. Marriage has not been legally available to same-sex couples since 2022. The Domestic Partnership Act 2017, assented to by the Governor of Bermuda in February 2018, replaced same-sex marriage with domestic partnerships for both same-sex and heterosexual couples, the reversal that made Bermuda the first jurisdiction to revoke marriage equality. Same-sex marriage was not permitted in July 2013.

In 2006 the Government attempted to ban Mark Anderson, also known as the drag queen Queen of Bermuda Sybil, from participating in a parade, stating that he contradicted local mores and sensitivities.
tangentialFactors:
Decriminalisation in 1994 divided the island at the time, with religious leaders divided and the Christian Coalition staging marches against the change.

Organised religious hostility toward visible same-sex visitors has been documented. Churches including the African Methodist Episcopal church protested a gay cruise on the Norwegian Dawn from New York to Bermuda on 12 July as incompatible with the word of God and the Christian moral fibre. A 2007 plan by LGBT R Family Vacations to visit Bermuda drew protest organized by about eighty churches as United by Faith, leading organizers to replace Bermuda and state that they did not want to expose children on board to that hatred while on vacation. The LGBT company Pied Piper has organized trips since 1990 without incident.

In November 2020 enforcement under the archaic obscene behaviour law led to a man charged and threatened with jail for importing DVDs of gay porn. The government spent approximately 150,000 pounds appealing the case after it was found unconstitutional.
localsOnly:
In February 2015 a Supreme Court ruling found direct discrimination on marital status and indirect discrimination on sexual orientation in the denial of an adoption application. As a result the Adoption of Children Act applies equally to married and non-married couples and same-sex couples may adopt.

The Bermuda Regiment is formed by conscription and does not discriminate on grounds of sexual orientation, with an official prohibition on discriminating against or harassing LGBT soldiers. Such conduct has been reported as tolerated by officers, to the extent one conscript described the Regiment as the most homophobic environment that exists.

Gay and bisexual men may donate blood with the Bermuda Hospitals Board if they have not had sex with another man in the past 12 months, with the same 12-month deferral for women who have sexual relations with men who have sex with men.
outOfScopeNotes:
Not sourced in the inventory are rules on gender marker change, entry and visa treatment of trans persons, screening that risks outing, bathroom and facilities law, access to gender-related care, hate-crime protection covering gender identity, and trans-specific violence with dates and outcomes. Those points remain unresolved for this dossier.

The inventory provides no documented statement about societal tolerance of transgender people specifically. Available descriptions of tolerance, bullying, venues and pride participation are framed around sexuality or LGBT generally, not transgender specifically, and are therefore not carried as findings about trans persons.
